subject.title: fix: provider usage accounting, retry/overflow classification, and output clamping

question: Should an unset Anthropic maxRetries preserve the documented SDK default, or should zero retries become the new package-level default for every caller?
rationale: This is an upgrade-sensitive provider API decision: outer OpenClaw retries justify disabling nested retries at an owning caller, but do not establish that all direct adapter and plugin consumers should lose the existing default.

options.title: Preserve the adapter default
options.body: Leave maxRetries undefined in the provider adapter and explicitly pass zero only from the OpenClaw caller that owns the outer retry policy.

options.title: Adopt zero globally
options.body: Make zero the intentional package default, update the public contract, and provide upgrade and real-runtime evidence for callers without outer retries.

recommendation.title: Preserve the adapter default
recommendation.body: Leave maxRetries undefined in the provider adapter and explicitly pass zero only from the OpenClaw caller that owns the outer retry policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch introduces the default change and bundles the outer-retry rationale, making the proposer the best available owner for this explicit contract choice.
